extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners evaluating or preparing ex parte reexamination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Deciding whether to order and how to process an ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302–304, including the substantive standard for a "substantial new question of patentability" (SNQ), what claims and prior art may be considered, and required content of the decision ordering reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for Deciding Request (3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether or not to reexamine must be made within 3 months following the filing date of a request. See 35 U.S.C. 303(a) and 37 CFR 1.515(a). If the 3-month period ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday within the District of Columbia, then the determination must be mailed by the preceding business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination to reexamine may be made at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent. See MPEP § 2240 and § 2283 for related timing rules for multiple copending reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing Standard — 'Substantial New Question of Patentability' (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence or absence of 'a substantial new question of patentability' determines whether or not reexamination is ordered. The meaning and scope is developed case-by-case using case law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art patents and printed publications raise an SNQ of at least one claim, then an SNQ is present unless the same question has already been decided in a final federal court holding, decided in an earlier concluded Office examination or review, or raised in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination. Issues involving 35 U.S.C. 325(d) must be brought to appropriate SPRS or CRU Director attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art Importance Test (reasonable examiner)
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior art patent or printed publication raises an SNQ where there is a substantial likelihood that a reasonable examiner would consider the prior art important in deciding whether or not the claim is patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the prior art would be considered important, the examiner should find an SNQ unless the same question has already been decided as to the claim in a final holding by a federal court or by the Office in an earlier concluded examination or review, or is raised in a pending reexamination/supplemental examination. If additional art is merely cumulative to art already fully considered, it may not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-part Necessary Test for SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: For an SNQ to be present it is necessary that: (A) the prior art patents and/or printed publications raise an SNQ regarding at least one claim (teaching such that a reasonable examiner would consider it important) and (B) the same question has not been decided by the Office earlier, raised in a pending reexamination/supplemental examination, or decided in a final federal court holding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary that a 'prima facie' case of unpatentability exist; SNQ may be present even if the examiner would not necessarily reject the claim as fully anticipated or obvious. See In re Etter for discussion on difference between SNQ and prima facie unpatentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: KSR Decision Does Not Alter SNQ Standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarification of the legal standard for obviousness in KSR International Co. v. Teleflex does not alter the legal standard for determining whether an SNQ exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See discussion in MPEP § 2216 for context; SNQ analysis remains under existing SNQ principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second or Subsequent Request Must Stand on Own Merits
rubrics_metrics.description: A second or subsequent request should be determined on its own merits without reference to the pending reexamination. The second/subsequent requester must independently provide an SNQ which is different from that raised in the pending reexamination for the claims in effect at the time of the determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision on second/subsequent request is based on the claims in effect at the time of determination (37 CFR 1.515(a)). If a different SNQ is not provided for the claims in effect, the second/subsequent request must be denied because statute authorizes reexamination only based on an SNQ affecting any claim of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Proposed New or Amended Claims in Subsequent Requests
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a second or subsequent request provides a 'different' SNQ based on the claims in effect, the request may also provide information directed to proposed new or amended claims in a pending reexamination to permit examination of the entire patent package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proper basis for subsequent reexamination is established, addressing proposed new/amended claims avoids waste and prevents patent owners from nominally amending claims to preclude a subsequent reexamination request during pendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Prior Favorable USPTO Decisions on Same 'Old Art'
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'substantial new question of patentability' is not raised by prior art presented in a reexamination request if the Office has previously considered the same question of patentability as to a claim and reached a favorable decision for the patent owner based on the same prior art patents or printed publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should check the patent file history to see if prior art now advanced was previously cited/considered in an earlier concluded examination or review, or raised in a pending reexamination or supplemental examination ('old art').

rubrics_metrics.name: Old Art Can Be Sole Basis for SNQ (post-Nov 2, 2002)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reliance on previously cited/considered art ('old art') does not necessarily preclude existence of an SNQ for reexamination ordered on or after November 2, 2002; determinations are fact-specific.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Old art may constitute sole basis for SNQ where it is presented/viewed in a new light or different way, e.g., in view of a material new argument or interpretation (including claim scope). Use form paragraph 22.01.01 when SNQ is based solely on old art and explain how the old art is applied and why it raises an SNQ. This form paragraph is used only the first time that 'already cited/considered' art is applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Adverse Office Decisions on Same Art Usually Indicate SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: A prior decision adverse to patentability of a claim by the Office based upon prior art patents or printed publications would usually mean that a substantially new question of patentability is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: an abandoned reissue application rejected on the claim may constitute such adverse decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Adverse Reissue Decisions Based on Non-Patent/Pub Grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Any prior adverse final decision by the Director or PTAB on a reissue application seeking the same patent will be considered when determining SNQ; however, to the extent such prior adverse final decision was based upon grounds other than patents or printed publications, it will not be a basis for determining whether an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider scope and grounds of prior adverse decisions when weighing whether SNQ exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions in Other Cases Involving Same Art — Weight Depends
rubrics_metrics.description: Decisions involving substantially identical patents or printed publications in other cases may be considered in determining whether an SNQ is raised, but the weight to be given such decisions depends upon the circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may consider out-of-case decisions but apply appropriate factual analysis rather than treating them as dispositive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of Final Federal Court Decision That Patent Not Proven Invalid
rubrics_metrics.description: A final court decision that a claim has not been proven invalid in view of the same or different prior art does not necessarily mean that no SNQ is present because Office and courts use different standards of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office may accord deference to district court factual findings, but the SNQ determination is made independently of the court's decision. See In re Swanson and In re Baxter for precedent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonfinal Court Holdings Not Controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonfinal holding of invalidity or unenforceability by the courts will not be controlling on the question of whether an SNQ is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only final judgments after all appeals have controlling effect concerning the existence of claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Court Holding of Invalidity/Unenforceability Is Controlling
rubrics_metrics.description: A final holding of invalidity or unenforceability, after all appeals, is controlling on the Office; a substantial new question of patentability would not be present as to claims finally held invalid or unenforceable because such claims no longer exist in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where claims are finally held invalid/unenforceable, they are effectively removed from consideration for SNQ purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims Considered — Claims in Effect at Time of Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The claims of the patent in effect at the time of the determination will be the basis for deciding whether an SNQ is present. 37 CFR 1.515(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office determination will generally be limited to review of the claim(s) for which reexamination was requested. Requester must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)); failure to do so generally precludes reexamination of that claim. The Office may, at its discretion, reexamine other claims or initiate reexamination on non-requested claims (35 U.S.C. 303(a)). Examiner should discuss all patent claims requested in the decision letter and limit discussion to whether an SNQ has been raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior Art That May Be Considered in Determination
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination whether an SNQ exists can be based upon any prior art patents or printed publications — the examiner is not limited to the art relied on in the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may base SNQ on art relied on in the request, a combination of that art and other art found elsewhere, or entirely different patents/printed publications. Examiner may consider patents/printed publications of record (e.g., submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 in compliance with 1.98). If additional prior art can be readily obtained to supply deficiencies in the request, the examiner may perform a limited additional search where there is reasonable likelihood of finding such art; search should be limited to area most likely to contain the deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Content When Granting Reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a request is granted, the examiner’s decision will: (A) identify all claims and issues, (B) identify the patents and/or printed publications relied on, and (C) provide a brief statement of the rationale supporting each new question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must identify at least one SNQ and explain how the prior art raises such. Examiner should indicate, insofar as possible, initial positions on all issues identified so patent owner and requester can comment. Prior art relied on should be listed on PTO form (e.g., PTO-892) if not already listed; supply copies only where not previously supplied to patent owner and requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Points the Decision Should Address (A–F)
rubrics_metrics.description: As to each SNQ identified, the decision should point out: (A) the prior art which adds some new teaching as to at least one claim; (B) what that new teaching is; (C) the claims that the new teaching is directed to; (D) that the new teaching was not previously considered/addressed or raised in pending proceedings; (E) that the new teaching is such that a reasonable examiner would consider it important; and (F) where relevant, why the patent or printed publication is deemed available against the patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MPEP § 2247.01 for examples. In simple cases examiner may adopt requester’s reasons for SNQ; if request does not indicate claims to be unpatentable, decision should phrase that SNQ is raised as to listed claims rather than saying requester considers claims unpatentable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision Is Not a Determination of Patentability
rubrics_metrics.description: In the decision on the request, the examiner will not decide, and no statement should be made as to, whether the claims are rejected over the patents and printed publications; the examiner only decides whether there is an SNQ to order reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The actual patentability issues are addressed during the reexamination examination stage; the decision letter should avoid making patentability rejections at the request-decision stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper Grounds for Reexamination Under 35 U.S.C. 302
rubrics_metrics.description: If arguments are raised by a requester as to grounds not based on patents or printed publications (e.g., public use or sale, abandonment under 35 U.S.C. 102(c) for first-to-invent prior art regime), such grounds are improper for reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302 and are not considered or commented upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to 37 CFR 1.552(c) for treatment; direct such issues elsewhere if raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and Extensions — Special Dispatch; No 1.136 Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions of time under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will not be permitted in ex parte reexamination proceedings because that provision applies only to an 'applicant' and not to parties in a reexamination proceeding. 35 U.S.C. 305 requires that ex parte reexamination proceedings 'will be conducted with special dispatch' (37 CFR 1.550(a)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions of time in ex parte reexamination are provided for in 37 CFR 1.550(c) only. Form paragraph 22.73 should be used for correspondence/inquiries and form paragraph 22.01 at beginning of each decision letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and Notice Procedures for Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After preparing and signing the decision, the reexamination file and decision are forwarded to the CRU Legal Instrument Examiner (LIE) for clerical processing; a copy of the decision is mailed to the patent owner and any third party, along with required copies of prior art documents; signed copy and copies of prior art are made of record in file history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice published in the Official Gazette under § 1.11(c) is constructive notice and ex parte reexamination will proceed. Use transmittal form PTOL-465 to forward copies to third-party requester. Electronic filing/transmission rules (37 CFR 1.8 and 1.6) and certificate-of-transmission requirements apply for timely filing of electronic correspondence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel Review, Conference, and Finalization of Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: After assignment to an examiner, the examiner prepares and sets up a panel review conference (per MPEP § 2271.01) to discuss issuance of the decision on the request. If conference confirms preliminary decision to grant, decision will be completed and signed by the examiner with two or more conferees initialing the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If CRU SPRS believes another Art Unit should examine the file, follow transfer procedures (MPEP § 2237). The substantive determination by the Director to institute reexamination is not subject to judicial review until a final agency decision in the reexamination proceeding has issued.
